newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

COFFEE - World market for December 4, 1996 - Robusta futures in London came under pressure all day but ended off lows after origin sellers retreated from falling prices. Front month January lost $16 per tonne to close at $1,323 while March gave up $20 to close at $1,272.

In New York arabica futures ended weaker for the fourth consecutive session as a round of fund long liquidation pushed prices to near six-week lows. December closed 1.50 cents/lb lower at 112.80 cents/lb, while March gave up 90 cents to close at 104.20 cents/lb.
The outer months lost between 25 and 100 points. Most analysts expect prices to ease further with no fundamental factors in sight to offset technical weakness.

ICO - Coffee exports to all destination by exporting members of the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) during October 1996 totalled 6.03 million 60-kg bags up from 4.84 million bags in September and 5.22 million bags in October 1995. That brought total exports in November/October 1995/96 up to 73.8 million bags up from 65.29 million bags in the year ago period.

Brazil's market share in November/October 1995/96 dropped sharply to 18.35 per cent from 23.68 per cent previously while Colombia's share increased marginally to 14.55 per cent from 14.42 per cent the previous year.

INTERNATIONAL - A leading Swiss coffee trader, Coffee Interlink SA, sees a tight 1996/97 coffee balance. They indicate the world's exportable crop will reach 73.7 million 60-kg bags, just barely sufficient to cover consumption of 73.5 million bags. They cited a supply gap of 10.5 million bags last year after a poor Brazilian crop. They expect Brazil alone to produce 9.9 million bags more this season.

NORWAY - Norway imported 48,130 bags of coffee in October 1996, 2.1 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 611,800 bags, 15 per cent more than was imported the same period 1995.

Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped sharply by 18 per cent to 662,100 bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Brazil (133,400 vs 208,500 bags) and Colombia (132,100 vs 115,200 bags).
